name: ANSI/IEEE active power indicator symbol
summary: IEEE-library wattmeter form for indicating active power from combined current and voltage inputs.
description: The active power indicator, usually labelled W or kW, needs both current and voltage inputs. On a single-line diagram it is drawn off the CT and VT secondaries of a feeder or generator, and on a schematic its current coils sit in series with the CT circuit while its voltage elements are connected across the VT secondary.

Whether the instrument measures one phase, three-phase three-wire or three-phase four-wire power is not visible from the circle. Element count, direction convention for import and export, and the CT and VT ratios used for scaling all need to be read from the meter data and connection diagram.
readingNotes: Trace both the CT and VT connections to the meter.
Check the number of measuring elements against the system wiring.
distinction: An active power indicator shows instantaneous watts; a recording wattmeter keeps a time record and a kWh meter integrates energy.
